rituals.name: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
rituals.title: THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT
rituals.goal: Ground steady attention; keep several explanations alive until new evidence separates them.
rituals.steps:
1. Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.
rituals.winReward: One event produced multiple testable possibilities instead of a single prediction dressed as certainty.
rituals.win: One event produced multiple testable possibilities instead of a single prediction dressed as certainty.
supportsArray: Check what you actually know; look for one missing fact.
Ask what else could fit; separate possibility from probability.
Delay major conclusions when upset; separate guess from evidence.
Ask what would disprove it; use recent, concrete evidence.
Delay the verdict; use current facts.
rituals.mindBend: Fortune telling feels convincing because the mind selects one future before reality has had a chance to vote.
rituals.formulaFlow: Keep Event → Invent → Predict Different → Earliest → Speak Plurals
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not multiply theories when an urgent practical response is already clear.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.title: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.goal: Notice the thought as mental activity, then keep doing what you chose; hold deeper quiet.
rituals.steps:
1. Put “I am noticing my mind produce…” before the thought. Say the whole sentence once at normal speed.
2. Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.
rituals.winReward: The thought remained present without deciding what your hands or attention did next.
rituals.win: The thought remained present without deciding what your hands or attention did next.
supportsArray: Start physically; shrink the first action.
Reward starting, not finishing; choose tiny action.
Cut the task; make it visible.
Skip extra setup; lower the first demand.
Begin while unsure; choose a rough beginning.

rituals.name: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
rituals.title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
rituals.goal: Keep deeper quiet: respect the warning in a thought without letting it sign the contract.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer: “I’m not signing this instruction.” Choose one action that reflects what matters to you while keeping any useful caution.
4. Respect the alarm; decline the contract.
rituals.winReward: You kept the useful caution and still chose one action that matched what matters.
rituals.win: You kept the useful caution and still chose one action that matched what matters.
supportsArray: Do not wait for motivation; name what matters today.
Use one priority; keep meaning practical.
Choose one value-led action; accept the trade-off.
Protect important time; use values to choose trade-offs.
Remove one conflict; pick one value for this decision.
rituals.mindBend: A protective thought can have a good intention and still give bad instructions.
rituals.formulaFlow: Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect

rituals.name: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
rituals.title: THOUGHT DEPARTURES
rituals.goal: Watch a thought arrive and leave without helping it stay or go; keep gentle stillness.
rituals.steps:
1. Place the thought on something imagined as moving: a bus, leaf, or subtitle.
2. Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one fixed visual point.
4. Another carrier may come; none owns the station.
rituals.winReward: The thought completed one imagined journey while your attention returned to something real.
rituals.win: The thought completed one imagined journey while your attention returned to something real.
supportsArray: Test the assumption; use a real example.
Ask what would disprove it; notice absolute words like always.
Look for one missing fact; use current facts.
Use recent, concrete evidence; ask what else could fit.
Separate guess from evidence; avoid treating guesses as facts.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can pass through awareness without needing an exit strategy from you.
rituals.formulaFlow: Place Thought → Watch Arrival → Return Eyes → Allow Departure

PAUSE
Stop imagery if it increases detachment from surroundings.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: NAME THE SERIES
rituals.title: NAME THE SERIES
rituals.goal: Enter steady pause: recognise the recurring story before treating today's episode as new evidence.
rituals.steps:
1. Ignore today’s plot for ten seconds.
2. Ask which recurring series it belongs to—‘Rejection Prediction’, ‘Everyone Is Ahead’, or ‘Fix It Now’. Give it a title and season number.
3. Then check if this episode contains new information or recycled footage.

rituals.name: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
rituals.title: COMMAND DOWNGRADE
rituals.goal: Turn an inner command into information you can choose around; hold gentle pause.
rituals.steps:
1. Hear the command exactly as it arrives: ‘Leave now,’ ‘Check again,’ ‘You must reply.’
2. Translate it into an urge: ‘I feel an urge to leave, check, or reply.’
3. Let the urge give you information without giving it authority.
rituals.winReward: 'Must' became an urge you could notice without automatically carrying it out.
rituals.win: 'Must' became an urge you could notice without automatically carrying it out.
supportsArray: Leave the trigger; make access harder.
Remember urges peak and fall; delay ten minutes.
Make access less convenient; avoid bargaining.
Tell someone early; use your hands.
Avoid bargaining with the urge; change locations.

rituals.formulaFlow: Picture Command → Downgrade It → Reject Authority

rituals.name: PASSENGER THOUGHT
rituals.title: PASSENGER THOUGHT
rituals.goal: Find steady quiet: complete one meaningful action while the unwanted thought rides along.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose one two-minute action that matters.
2. Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
3. Hold hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks.

rituals.name: CAMERA FIRST, CAPTION SECOND
rituals.title: CAMERA FIRST, CAPTION SECOND
rituals.goal: Steady anchored focus: separate what a camera could record from the meaning you add afterward.
rituals.steps:
1. For fifteen seconds, collect camera data: colour, movement, sound, pressure, position.
2. Then say the event using only that footage.
3. Now add the meaning separately and label it CAPTION.
4. Keep both; never confuse their sources.

rituals.name: ENTER THE ACTION
rituals.title: ENTER THE ACTION
rituals.goal: Re-enter an ordinary activity through your senses instead of demanding perfect focus — hold quiet pause.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.

rituals.title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
rituals.goal: Enter deeper quiet: decide which thought deserves attention instead of letting every thought enter.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice the next thought without following it.
2. Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Give the chosen category five slow counts; let the others wait without argument.
4. After five counts, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.

rituals.name: THE 2% SOFTENING
rituals.title: THE 2% SOFTENING
rituals.goal: Test whether a tiny believable softening changes the body's defensive setting; quiet steady pace.
rituals.steps:
1. Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by two percent.
2. Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold it while resting your gaze on one neutral visual point.
4. Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.
rituals.winReward: One facial area eased slightly and you noticed whether defence shifted at all.
rituals.win: One facial area eased slightly and you noticed whether defence shifted at all.

Reduce extra stimulation; avoid symptom searching.
Unclench your jaw and shoulders; use ordinary surroundings.
Keep movements gentle; loosen your shoulders.
rituals.mindBend: The body reads your own expression as part of the environment. Even a tiny change can alter the signal it receives.

rituals.name: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
rituals.title: PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD
rituals.goal: Hold steady pause: use a slow movement sequence to prove your body can follow deliberate instructions.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and shift your gaze.
2. Do A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Do C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, restart instead of speeding up.
4. Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the code stop.
rituals.winReward: You completed the pattern forward and backward without speeding through a mistake.
rituals.win: You completed the pattern forward and backward without speeding through a mistake.
supportsArray: Sip water if it helps; wait out the surge.

Reduce extra stimulation; let breathing stay natural.
Give the surge time to pass; let breaths happen.
Loosen your shoulders; look at ordinary objects nearby.

rituals.formulaFlow: Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control

PAUSE

rituals.name: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
rituals.title: THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE
rituals.goal: Interrupt momentum long enough to choose the smallest safe move — settle deeper quiet.
rituals.steps:
1. Stop every nonessential movement.
2. Take one physical step back.
3. Observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse.
4. Proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Do not negotiate with momentum between letters.
rituals.winReward: Facts, sensations, and impulse were noticed before your next action happened.
rituals.win: Facts, sensations, and impulse were noticed before your next action happened.
supportsArray: Avoid bargaining; change locations.
Tell someone if the urge spikes; leave the trigger.
Change rooms if possible; delay ten minutes.
Do one incompatible activity; make access harder.
Ride the peak; avoid bargaining with the urge.
rituals.mindBend: Impulses gain power from speed. One physical step back creates time for judgment to re-enter.
rituals.formulaFlow: Stop Nonessential → Take Physical → Observe Facts → Proceed Safely → Skip Negotiation

rituals.name: ONE FOOT HERE, EYES OPEN
rituals.title: ONE FOOT HERE, EYES OPEN
rituals.goal: Enter brief quiet; re-anchor in the current room without pulling more detail from the past.
rituals.steps:
1. Press one foot into the floor and keep both eyes open.
2. Look at each room corner and name one visible difference.
3. Say your current age without describing the earlier event.
4. Move farther from anything that increases the memory alarm.
5. Contact a safe person if present-time orientation stays weak.
rituals.winReward: Your foot, open eyes, current age, and room cues made the present easier to locate.
rituals.win: Your foot, open eyes, current age, and room cues made the present easier to locate.
supportsArray: Keep your eyes open if safer; hold something familiar.
Keep the room comfortably lit; contact someone you trust.
Choose gentle, ordinary movement; stop if you feel less present.
Stop if less present; name today's date.
Feel your feet; avoid forced memories.

This is grounding only, not trauma treatment.

rituals.name: NO FAVOURITE SENSATION
rituals.title: NO FAVOURITE SENSATION
rituals.goal: Give pleasant, unpleasant, dull, and vivid sensations the same brief welcome; find steady anchor.
rituals.steps:

3. When preference reaches to grip or reject, include that movement too.
4. End by noticing the whole room at once.
rituals.winReward: Preference itself became another event in the field instead of deciding what had to stay or leave.
rituals.win: Preference itself became another event in the field instead of deciding what had to stay or leave.

Use the same replacement repeatedly; make the old habit harder.
Notice the trigger; delay the routine.
rituals.mindBend: Gripping and rejecting are extra movements added to sensation — noticing those movements reveals what the raw experience was doing first.
rituals.formulaFlow: Let Field → Pleasant → Include Movement → End Whole

rituals.name: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
rituals.title: EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND
rituals.goal: Find simple anchor; move from the whole moment to the breath, then back out to wider awareness.
rituals.steps:
1. First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.
rituals.winReward: Attention narrowed around breathing and reopened to body plus surrounding space before you moved on.

Eat, drink, or rest if needed; use plain language.

rituals.mindBend: Narrow focus and wide awareness are both tools. Flexibility comes from being able to change the size of attention on purpose.

rituals.title: RAIN WITHOUT THE UMBRELLA
rituals.goal: Acknowledge what is here, meet it kindly, and remember it is not all of you; steady quiet body.

1. Recognise what is here.
2. Allow this moment of it to exist.
3. Investigate with one kind question about body or need.
4. Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
5. Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.
rituals.winReward: The experience was recognised, allowed, gently investigated, and placed inside a larger sense of self.

Use simple words for the problem; slow physical pace.
Notice what changed physically; delay the message.
Rest before deciding; use plain language.

rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Skip investigation when acute distress requires grounding first.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
rituals.fullRitual:
PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Acknowledge what is here, meet it kindly, and remember it is not all of you; steady quiet body.

STEPS
1. Recognise what is here.
2. Allow this moment of it to exist.
3. Investigate with one kind question about body or need.
4. Notice that the experience is present but not the whole of you.
5. Move through R–A–I–N once; resolution is not a required fifth letter.

WIN
The experience was recognised, allowed, gently investigated, and placed inside a larger sense of self.

MIND BEND
Acceptance is not a fifth step called resolution. Sometimes the shift is simply ending the demand that the experience disappear.

FORMULA FLOW
Recognise → Allow Moment → Question About → Experience → Move R

SAFETY
PAUSE
Skip investigation when acute distress requires grounding first.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
rituals.title: FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP
rituals.goal: Quiet anchored signal: walk slowly enough to notice the four physical parts of each step.
rituals.steps:
1. Slow enough to separate lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
2. Follow those four events through several steps.
3. When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
4. Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.
rituals.winReward: Attention rejoined the foot at its current phase whenever thought pulled away.
rituals.win: Attention rejoined the foot at its current phase whenever thought pulled away.
supportsArray: Take a short break; return to one target.

Put the phone out of reach; reduce background noise.
Close extra tabs; protect one focus block.
Use one screen; clear visual clutter.
rituals.mindBend: A moving body provides a restart point every second — you do not need to recover the moment you missed.

rituals.name: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
rituals.title: LISTEN PAST THE SOUND
rituals.goal: Follow a sound all the way into silence without keeping it alive in memory — anchor steady focus.
rituals.steps:
1. Ring, play, or notice a safe sustained sound.
2. Follow its decay with precision until you cannot locate any remainder.
3. Stay with the silence that receives it, not with memory of the tone.
4. Let the next surroundings sound end the practice.
rituals.winReward: The tone disappeared completely and the next real sound, not the remembered one, ended the practice.
rituals.win: The tone disappeared completely and the next real sound, not the remembered one, ended the practice.
supportsArray: Reset after slips; move the cue.
Expect slips and restart quickly; reduce easy access to triggers.
Notice the first automatic moment; make the new habit easier.
Remove easy access; change the environment first.
Keep replacement easy; interrupt the sequence.
rituals.mindBend: Silence is not the absence of attention. It becomes perceptible when you stop replacing a finished sound with its mental echo.
rituals.formulaFlow: Play Safe → Follow Decay → Stay Silence → Let Surroundings

PAUSE
Avoid intense volume or tones associated with distress.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: NOTICE THE NOTICING
rituals.title: NOTICE THE NOTICING
rituals.goal: Steady quiet moment; notice a sensation, then notice that knowing is already happening.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose any sensation.
2. First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with knowing rather than searching for a separate thing called awareness.
4. Return by naming one visible fact.
rituals.winReward: Attention rested with the fact of awareness without needing to locate a separate object called awareness.
rituals.win: Attention rested with the fact of awareness without needing to locate a separate object called awareness.
supportsArray: Silence nonessential notifications; close what you do not need.
Use a short focus block; take a real screen break.
Use one window at a time; return after interruptions.
Reduce background noise; keep one task visible.
Reduce nearby noise; use one screen.
rituals.mindBend: You never have to manufacture the knowing of an experience; the search for awareness happens inside awareness already.

rituals.name: THE BREATH HINGE
rituals.title: THE BREATH HINGE
rituals.goal: Feel the natural turning points of breathing without holding them open; quiet steady space.
rituals.steps:
1. Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.
2. Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
4. Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.
rituals.winReward: Both breath hinges were noticed lightly and several later breaths were allowed to pass unwatched.
rituals.win: Both breath hinges were noticed lightly and several later breaths were allowed to pass unwatched.
supportsArray: Stop body scanning; use ordinary surroundings.
Let breaths happen; loosen your shoulders.
Avoid repeated pulse checking; stay somewhere physically safe.
Keep your body supported; sit somewhere safe.
Look at ordinary objects nearby; unclench your jaw and shoulders.
rituals.mindBend: A transition can be felt without being controlled. The breath changes direction before conscious effort has to manage the switch.
rituals.formulaFlow: Follow Inhale → Leave Free → Change → Allow Breaths
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Leave the hinge alone if waiting creates retention or air hunger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING
rituals.title: WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING
rituals.goal: Steady anchored body: follow a sound toward the point where 'outside' becomes hearing.
rituals.steps:
1. Listen to a sustained, gentle sound.
2. Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable.
3. When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly.
rituals.winReward: The boundary between vibration out there and auditory experience in here became less definite for a moment.
rituals.win: The boundary between vibration out there and auditory experience in here became less definite for a moment.
supportsArray: Wait before sending messages; do one steadying action.
Let intensity fall; check the facts separately.
Check basic needs; give the feeling time to move.
Notice body tension; delay the message.
Name the feeling plainly; use plain language.
rituals.mindBend: Hearing feels like a simple outside-to-inside event until attention looks for the exact border and cannot find a clean line.
rituals.formulaFlow: Listen Sustained → Follow Apparent → Rest Briefly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
rituals.title: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
rituals.goal: Widen your visual field enough to hold outer space and inner contraction together — find quiet pause.
rituals.steps:
1. Gaze softly into open sky or another unobstructed safe field.
2. Release pinpoint focus and include the edges of vision.
3. Without forcing calm, compare the width outside with the contraction inside.

rituals.goal: Quiet steady mind: notice wanting before the object takes over the whole experience.

rituals.title: WATCH PLEASURE LEAVE CLEANLY
rituals.goal: Settle deeper stillness; let a pleasant sensation fade completely without immediately reaching for another dose.

rituals.name: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
rituals.title: NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST
rituals.goal: Quiet still moment; release the inner pull or push around an experience before deciding what to do.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
2. Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.

Choose your own measure; track progress by your values.
Use your own priorities; name one thing already working.
rituals.mindBend: Attraction and aversion can feel like properties of the thing itself even though they are movements happening in your response.
rituals.formulaFlow: Check Pull → Relax → Let Content → Act According

rituals.title: WHO RECEIVED THAT THOUGHT?
rituals.goal: Quiet still mind: follow the question of who received a thought without forcing an answer.
rituals.steps:

rituals.name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
rituals.title: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER
rituals.goal: Find quiet anchor: put blended feelings back into the order they actually arrived.
rituals.steps:
1. Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.
rituals.winReward: Each emotion was linked to its own cue, making the sequence clearer without needing a bigger story.

rituals.title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.ritual_name: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
rituals.goal: Let one thought end without immediately filling the empty beat with another; find deeper stillness.
rituals.steps:
1. Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count the gap only after it is over.

Skip extra setup; enter through easy work.

keywords: You keep replaying the same question

display.title: DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT
display.goal: Let one thought end without immediately filling the empty beat with another; find deeper stillness.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count the gap only after it is over.
display.win: A real gap appeared before the next thought arrived on its own, even if it lasted only a fraction.
display.mindBend: The mind can hide silence by commenting on it. The first post-gap thought can make the gap seem absent.
display.formulaFlow: Wait Thought → Empty → Rest Duration → Let Thought → Count Gap

rituals.name: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
rituals.title: PAY FOR THE NEXT LAP
rituals.goal: Steady anchored attention: make another thinking lap pay for the time it takes from real life.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the exact question you want one more thinking lap to answer. One sentence only.
2. Choose what those three minutes will replace: rest, a message, food, movement, work, or a decision. Say the trade plainly.
3. If the trade is worth it, set three minutes and think only about the named question. If not, close the lap now.
4. When the clock ends, stop without buying another lap. Do the displaced activity or deliberately let it go.
rituals.winReward: The exact question and its trade-off were named before three minutes of thinking were either bought or declined.
rituals.win: The exact question and its trade-off were named before three minutes of thinking were either bought or declined.
supportsArray: Return to one physical task; leave unsolved questions.
End the replay; set a clear stopping point.
Change rooms if possible; stop solving the unsolvable.
Name one useful action; ask if any new information exists.
Stop repeated review; return to current task.
rituals.mindBend: Mental time feels free because its cost is invisible — naming what it replaces turns rumination into a real transaction.
rituals.formulaFlow: Name Lap → Price Trade → Buy Three → Close Toll

PAUSE

rituals.title: IMAGINE THE FEELING’S SHAPE
rituals.goal: Steady slower pace: give the feeling a shape, then change one visual feature and notice the effect.

2. Add a boundary, pressure source, and possible exit route.

rituals.name: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
rituals.title: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE
rituals.goal: Quiet rising noise: put one memory segment into past tense while inserting present facts between loaded lines.
rituals.steps:
1. Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
2. After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: your present location, the current year, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish with: ‘That ended; this moment is different.’
rituals.winReward: The retelling repeatedly returned to current place, year, and available choice before ending in today's reality.
rituals.win: The retelling repeatedly returned to current place, year, and available choice before ending in today's reality.
supportsArray: Slow physical pace; do one steadying action.
Lower stimulation for a minute; name the feeling plainly.
Eat, drink, or rest if needed; separate feeling from fact.
Rest before deciding; lower nearby noise.
Name the emotion; check the facts separately.
rituals.mindBend: Grammar can carry time: past-tense language plus current facts helps stop an old event from borrowing the present tense.
rituals.formulaFlow: Use Happened → Ground Between → Finish Moment
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not retell alone if the memory overwhelms sense of where you are.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
rituals.title: THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS
rituals.goal: Ground quiet pace; put past actions, present repairs, and future prevention back into their correct time zones.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture three time zones: PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Place completed actions in PAST, available repair in PRESENT, and prevention plans in FUTURE.
3. Move any item that belongs to the wrong time zone.
4. Do only one PRESENT task now.
rituals.winReward: Misplaced tasks moved to the right period, leaving one genuinely present action to do now.
rituals.win: Misplaced tasks moved to the right period, leaving one genuinely present action to do now.
supportsArray: Lower standards briefly; choose a rough beginning.
Do the easiest useful part; start with one minute.
Prepare first; start physically.
Set a two-minute timer; prepare the task in advance.
Lower the first demand; make it visible.
rituals.mindBend: Guilt and worry often mix time zones. A past event cannot be repaired by a future plan that never becomes a present action.
rituals.formulaFlow: Make Zones → Complete Actions → Reassign → Do Job
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use time ownership to evade current accountability for earlier harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.title: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.ritual_name: PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM
rituals.goal: Restore the real time distance between events that currently feel piled together; hold brief pause.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
2. Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.
rituals.winReward: Older events moved back along the timeline, and one fact belonging only to today regained its proper place.
rituals.win: Older events moved back along the timeline, and one fact belonging only to today regained its proper place.
supportsArray: Ignore imagined regret; reduce the options.
Keep new facts separate; limit the options.
Choose the option you can support; commit once chosen.
Choose reversible first; set a deadline.
Ask what failure would cost; stop extra research.

rituals.formulaFlow: Date Events → Scale Distance → Present → Recheck Urgency

rituals.name: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
rituals.title: DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE
rituals.goal: Quiet steady moment; turn identity verdicts into temporary processes that can change under conditions.
rituals.steps:
1. Restate ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is.
2. Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’.

rituals.name: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
rituals.title: ZOOM LENS TRAINING
rituals.goal: Settle steady stillness; practise moving attention between tiny detail and the whole scene.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture one simple shape.
2. Spend ten slow counts on one tiny feature.
3. Spend ten counts on the whole shape and the space around it.
4. Move back to detail, then choose the view that best fits your task.

rituals.title: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
rituals.ritual_name: THE PRICE OF KEEPING THIS SELF
rituals.goal: Measure what an identity lets you do, blocks, and demands before deciding whether it still serves you — hold steady quiet.

rituals.name: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
rituals.title: CALL THE INNER COUNCIL
rituals.goal: Let different inner needs speak once, then give coordination to the part protecting the whole system — quiet extra noise.
rituals.steps:
1. Give each self-state an imagined place.
2. One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Appoint an inner coordinator whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
4. Let that coordinator combine, delay, or reject proposals while acknowledging every need.

rituals.name: BORROW A PRESENT VOICE
rituals.title: BORROW A PRESENT VOICE
rituals.goal: Anchor quiet pace; use a real present-day support voice without imagining the past scene.
rituals.steps:
1. Name one safe person, service, or professional you can contact today.
2. Choose one sentence they would realistically say about what you need now.
3. Repeat only that present-day sentence once; do not picture the past event.
4. Decide whether to contact them or return to a neutral task.

display.title: BORROW A PRESENT VOICE
display.goal: Anchor quiet pace; use a real present-day support voice without imagining the past scene.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Name one safe person, service, or professional you can contact today.
2. Choose one sentence they would realistically say about what you need now.
3. Repeat only that present-day sentence once; do not picture the past event.
4. Decide whether to contact them or return to a neutral task.
display.win: A believable present-day support line replaced solitary looping with a real next source of help.
display.mindBend: Support does not have to enter the old scene to matter. A real voice can change what happens next in the present.

rituals.title: RELATIONSHIP DATA, NOT ONE BIG FEELING
rituals.ritual_name: RELATIONSHIP DATA, NOT ONE BIG FEELING
rituals.goal: Anchor steady signal: review a relationship as separate events, patterns, context, repair attempts, and outcomes.
rituals.steps:

rituals.title: APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS
rituals.goal: Settle gentle stillness: judge an apology by what is acknowledged, what changes, and what prevents the same harm returning.
rituals.steps:

2. Decide what evidence would show each sign over time.
3. Judge the apology by those signs, not by the emotion of the moment.
rituals.winReward: The apology was measured against three visible signs of repair instead of the feeling of the moment.
rituals.win: The apology was measured against three visible signs of repair instead of the feeling of the moment.

Use simple words for the problem; delay the message.
Separate feeling from fact; notice body tension.
Do one steadying action; check the facts separately.
rituals.mindBend: Remorse can feel strong before behaviour changes. Repair becomes believable when something is actually different afterward.

rituals.goal: Steady quiet pace; choose the smallest contact dose that preserves both connection and steadiness.
rituals.steps:

3. Review afterward using your body and behaviour, not guilt.

rituals.name: WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?
rituals.title: WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?
rituals.ritual_name: WHAT SPECIES OF UNKNOWN IS THIS?
rituals.goal: Match each kind of unknown with the response that actually fits it — settle brief quiet.
rituals.steps:
1. Sort the unknown into one of four types: answerable now, answerable later, influenceable, or unknowable.
2. Match it with checking, scheduling, action, or acceptance.
3. Do not use one type’s solution on another.
rituals.winReward: Each unknown was matched with a fitting response instead of borrowing the wrong solution.
rituals.win: Each unknown was matched with a fitting response instead of borrowing the wrong solution.
supportsArray: Accept a small margin of risk; use a decision deadline.
Limit checking; accept small risk.
Stop reopening choices; delay reassurance.
Leave one question unanswered; set a limit on checking.
Ask what is controllable now; act with uncertainty.
rituals.mindBend: Different unknowns need different tools. Research cannot solve the unknowable, and acceptance cannot answer something you can simply check.
rituals.formulaFlow: Classify → Apply Move → Use Category

PAUSE

rituals.title: PLAN BOTH BRANCHES

rituals.steps:

rituals.name: PARKING RULE
rituals.title: PARKING RULE
rituals.goal: When several tasks feel equally urgent, choose one and silence the strongest competitor — find present anchor.
rituals.steps:
1. Notice when pressure makes several tasks feel equally urgent.
2. Choose which item matters more right now.
3. Name the distraction once, then mute it.
4. Start the chosen task.
5. Name the requests you are parking.
rituals.winReward: One task became active while parked requests stopped presenting themselves as simultaneous emergencies.
rituals.win: One task became active while parked requests stopped presenting themselves as simultaneous emergencies.
supportsArray: Separate urgent from important; choose top three.
Remove duplicate commitments; match real capacity.

Finish one before adding another; cut what cannot fit.
Leave empty space; protect one priority.
rituals.mindBend: Equal urgency is often an attention illusion. Once one task is chosen, the others can become future items instead of current threats.

rituals.title: MOTIVATION OR FRICTION?
rituals.goal: Find out whether disengagement is really low motivation or a fixable blocker before judging the person — find steady stillness.
rituals.steps:
1. Name only what you can observe: late replies, low output, silence, missed steps—not “doesn’t care.”
2. List three possible blockers such as unclear work, overload, a skill gap, conflict, low value, or low energy.
3. Pick one question that could separate low motivation from a practical blocker.
4. Ask it neutrally, or prepare to ask: “What is making this hard to move?”
5. Set one small next step from what you learn.
rituals.winReward: You replaced a motivation guess with a testable explanation and a fair next move.

supportsArray: Set one follow-up date; leave work delegated.

display.goal: Find deeper quiet: break the cue-to-access pathway and keep live support close during the craving.

safety.raw:
PAUSE
Move away from access, money, apps, substances, traffic, or other hazards. Contact a trusted person or qualified service if the urge feels difficult to manage safely. Call Triple Zero (000) for immediate danger.
This is brief self-help, not treatment or emergency care.

rituals.name: GROUND BEFORE THE MESSAGE
rituals.title: GROUND BEFORE THE MESSAGE
rituals.goal: Lower the body's speed enough to choose a steady message instead of a pressured one; ground still moment.
rituals.steps:
1. Let the first pressure pass without acting.
2. Slow your body one notch.
3. Separate the event from the meaning you fear.
4. Say how much capacity is genuinely available right now.
5. Choose one steady sentence you can send without hurrying.
rituals.winReward: The facts, feared meaning, and available capacity separated before one sendable sentence was chosen.
rituals.win: The facts, feared meaning, and available capacity separated before one sendable sentence was chosen.
supportsArray: Return when your body settles; use one clear request.

Use one request; avoid adding old grievances.
Name the exact issue; do not send the message yet.
Stick to current facts; name the issue.

rituals.name: TREAT THIS AS MEDICAL NOW
rituals.title: TREAT THIS AS MEDICAL NOW
rituals.playTime: ACT NOW — MOVE TO LIVE SUPPORT
rituals.goal: If symptoms after stopping or cutting down alcohol or drugs are severe or worsening, get urgent medical care.
rituals.steps:
1. Stop any breathing exercises, movement exercises, or mental exercises now.
2. Sit somewhere safe and do not drive yourself for care.
3. Call 000 for severe symptoms or symptoms that are getting worse quickly.
4. Tell responders what you used, any medicines, your symptoms, and when they started.
5. Stay with another person so changes can be noticed.

rituals.goal: Hold steady stillness: set an unsolvable question down and take a step that does not depend on its answer.

display.title: THE SECOND VIEW FIRST
display.goal: Create one beat of distance before treating a result as the only possible interpretation; ground soft attention.
display.numberedSteps:
1. Slow this moment by one beat.
2. Say only the result aloud; leave the sequence alone.
display.win: Only the result was named; the surrounding sequence was not rebuilt to force an interpretation.
display.mindBend: Certainty often enters through narrative sequence: once every step is arranged to support one conclusion, alternatives disappear. Naming only the result reopens the frame.
display.formulaFlow: Hold Question → Recall Outcome

rituals.name: WHO YOU CHOOSE NEXT
rituals.title: WHO YOU CHOOSE NEXT
rituals.goal: Hold deeper stillness; keep a disturbing thought separate from identity and let the next chosen action represent you instead.
rituals.steps:
1. Catch the thought without explaining it.
2. Say, “My mind produced this; it is not my biography.”
3. Name one value you want to stand for in the next minute—kind, honest, patient, careful, brave, or another word that fits.
4. Do one ten-second action that matches that principle.
5. Leave the thought unanswered and continue with the action.
rituals.winReward: A value was named and a ten-second action expressed it while the thought remained unanswered.
